transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, your clinical conversational agent. I'm calling to follow up on your cataract surgery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start doing light gardening, such as brisk walking, gardening, or gentle cycling, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's best to avoid heavy exercise, lifting heavy objects, or activities that might get water in your eyes, especially in the first month. You can also go back to golf or tennis after 1 week with protective eyewear. Would you like to ask another question?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that information! My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should continue to use your eye drops as was prescribed. If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide some more. And if you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for glaucoma, or for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise. You can start using them as directed, but if you have any questions about how to use them or when to stop, it's always best to check with your GP or care team. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light right now. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal to be a bit sensitive to light as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. However, if it's significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity, especially if your eye is also red and painful, we may need to assess this further. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend just wearing sunglasses when you're going outside. Would you like to ask another question?
transcript.delivered: It's normal to be a bit sensitive to light as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. However, if it's significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity, especially if your eye is also red and painful, we may need to assess this further.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common for the vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation. But this should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse or blurry, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay. It's also worth noting that if you had a standard lens put in, you might need reading glasses or varifocals for reading, as most lenses are for distance vision. Would you like to ask another question?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all the questions I had. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! It was my pleasure to help. I'm glad I could answer your questions about your cataract surgery recovery. Do you feel like all your questions have been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. You answered everything I needed to know. Thanks again!
